note: Which hosted model sits behind each engineering tier.
Hosted only. The target VPS is small, and a local model there would be slow enough
that engineers stop using the tool - the same outcome as not building it.
Override one tier for a single session without editing this file:
$env:HM_OI_FAST_MODEL   = 'openai/gpt-5-nano'
$env:HM_OI_NORMAL_MODEL = 'openai/gpt-5-mini'
$env:HM_OI_DEEP_MODEL   = 'openai/gpt-5.4-mini'
Model strings are litellm-style: '<provider>/<model>'. Anything litellm supports
works, so anthropic/... or gemini/... are valid if the key allows them.
IMPORTANT when changing a model: Open Interpreter is a tool-calling client, and a
model that will not accept a tool call does nothing here at all. Check a new model
before trusting it. gpt-5.6-luna - the model the product itself uses - fails: it
rejects tools whenever a reasoning effort is set, and litellm sets one for it
automatically, so every turn returns HTTP 400.
The api key comes from HM_OI_API_KEY. It does NOT fall back to OPENAI_API_KEY
unless HM_OI_ALLOW_SHARED_KEY=1 is set on purpose. The product's key pays for
customer turns, and its spend is reported as customer spend; engineering sessions
billed to it would corrupt the only number that says whether the product's AI cost
is under control.
The prices below are a rough guide for choosing between tiers by hand. They are
never used as a billing figure - the provider's own accounting is authoritative.
Check them against your account before relying on them.

fast.use_for: finding files, locating tests, reading logs, simple classification

normal.use_for: routine bug investigation, planning, writing tests, small fixes

deep.use_for: architecture, security, Setup Chat semantics, repeated failed fixes, high-risk change
